page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4n family. It features 8 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 62.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. This configuration is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require dedicated compute resources without the overhead of shared-core architectures.

This server type does not include integrated local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached block storage. Additionally, the instance does not feature any graphics processing units (GPUs) and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highmem-8 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute allocation, making it suitable for workloads where memory capacity is the primary constraint rather than raw processing power. Appropriate workloads for this profile include medium-sized databases, in-memory caching systems, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
